title: Hopf, Hecke, Quantum-Group, and Braid Interfaces

items.title: The rational spin-1/2 spectral R-matrix
items.statement: For V=C^2 with its ordered basis, define the flip P(e_a tensor e_b)=e_b tensor e_a and R(u)=uI+iP; define the checked and three-leg operators by the corresponding basis permutations.
items.strategy: Fix the field, tensor-product convention, standard tensor bases, flip, parameter, and checked operator.
items.axiom_use: None; all maps are explicitly defined on finite bases.

sources.title: L. D. Faddeev, How Algebraic Bethe Ansatz Works for Integrable Model

items.title: The rational spin-1/2 spectral R-matrix satisfies Yang-Baxter
items.statement: For all x,y,z in C, R_12(x-y)R_13(x-z)R_23(y-z)=R_23(y-z)R_13(x-z)R_12(x-y), and the corresponding checked operators satisfy the additive braid-form spectral identity.
items.strategy: Verify the permutation products on the tensor basis, then expand both sides in the six permutation operators.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof checks a finite explicit basis and uses no choice.

sources.title: L. D. Faddeev, How Algebraic Bethe Ansatz Works for Integrable Model
Pavel Etingof and Mykola Semenyakin, A Brief Introduction to Quantum Groups

title: Hopf, Hecke, Quantum-Group, and Braid Interfaces: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Rank-one Hecke specializations can be semisimple or nonsemisimple
items.statement: For W=S_2 in the local normalized Hecke convention, H_2(i) is C[epsilon]/(epsilon^2) and is nonsemisimple, while H_2(1)=H_2(-1)=C[T]/(T^2-1) is semisimple.
items.strategy: Specialize the rank-one quadratic relation and prove both regular-module outcomes directly.
items.axiom_use: None; all algebra and module decompositions are explicit and finite.

sources.title: Meinolf Geck, Modular Representations of Hecke Algebras
sources.locator: Sections 2 and 4.1, PDF pp. 5–7 and 15–16; source normalization is translated explicitly in the local Hecke convention.

items.title: The rational spectral R-matrix has singular parameter values
items.statement: The symmetric and antisymmetric eigenvalues of R(u) are u+i and u-i; the family is singular exactly at u=±i, while the checked u=0 operator is iI and yields a braid-group character.
items.strategy: Diagonalize the flip on the symmetric and antisymmetric subspaces and check the parameterized identity at a singular triple.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses an explicit four-dimensional matrix and finite-dimensional linear algebra.
